requirements.note: Bubbles: mine blue on the right, Sam's grey on the left, oldest at top. Messages-style date headings ('Sun, Oct 18 3:16 AM', 'Today 11:04 PM'). Opens at the newest message.
Send works and the thread stays at the bottom; the composer clears. Send stays disabled for empty or whitespace-only text. The Return key also sends.

The composer sits on the keyboard and the newest messages stay visible. Dragging the thread dismisses the keyboard. At the largest text size the composer grows to about 6 lines and covers most of the thread.
A 'Sam is typing…' bubble appears in the thread and 'typing…' under the title. About 2 s later Sam replies 'Love that'.
Long-press opens the system context menu with Copy and Delete. Copy pasted correctly; Delete removed the message and the deletion survived a relaunch.
Scrolls smoothly to the first message (Jul 1). A round jump-to-newest button appears when scrolled up and returns to the bottom.
Sent messages and Sam's replies survive a relaunch.

bugs: At the largest text size with the keyboard up, the jump-to-newest button is pushed up over the navigation bar, next to the title.
tells: The 'S' avatar sits in a glass button at the left of the nav bar, where a back button goes, and it does nothing. Messages centres the avatar above the name.
The send button is a separate glass circle outside the text field; iOS Messages puts it inside the field.
At the largest text size the composer grows without limit, to about 6 lines, and covers the thread.
The jump-to-newest button overlaps message bubbles; minor.
A.scroll: Native-feeling scrolling: no blank rows, pop-in or tearing in mid-fling frames. Reached the first message cleanly and the scroll indicator stayed steady (39 pages throughout).

requirements.note: Bubbles on the correct sides, oldest at top, date headings where the day changes. Headings include the year ('Oct 18, 2026 at 3:16 AM'). Opens at the newest message.
Send works and the thread stays at the bottom; the composer clears. Send stays disabled for whitespace-only text. Return inserts a new line, which is acceptable.
The composer stays above the keyboard and the newest messages stay visible. Dragging the thread dismisses the keyboard. At the largest text size the composer is capped at 2 lines and scrolls.
A 'Sam is typing…' bubble appears, then Sam replies ('👍' or 'Sounds good!') about 2 s later.
Long-press opens the system context menu with Copy and Delete. Copy pasted correctly; Delete removed the message and the deletion survived a relaunch.
Reaches the first message (Jul 1). A chevron jump-to-newest button appears when scrolled up and works.
Sent messages and replies survive a relaunch.

bugs: A frame captured mid-fling showed a rendering tear: fragments of a blue bubble drawn as broken horizontal strips above a message.
tells: Date headings always include the current year ('Oct 21, 2026 at 5:56 AM'); Messages shows 'Wed, Oct 21 at 5:56 AM' or 'Today'.
History loads in chunks while scrolling up: the scroll indicator's page count grew from 26 to 40, so the scroll thumb shifts as you go.
The jump-to-newest chevron button is a small hand-drawn circle that overlaps bubbles.
The nav bar shows no avatar and no 'typing' status; plainer than Messages.
B.scroll: Mostly smooth, and it reaches the first message. However, history loads in chunks while scrolling, so the scroll thumb shifts, and one mid-fling frame showed a torn bubble.

why: Both meet every requirement with system context menus, typing indicators, persistence and a jump-to-newest button, and they look nearly the same. A's scrolling was steadier: no chunked loading and no rendering tear. Its date headings and 'typing…' status in the title look more like Messages. A's large-text composer overgrowth, which pushes the jump button over the nav bar, is a smaller cost than B's scrolling glitches.
